# Similarweb.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/similarweb-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/similarweb-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects property listing data from Similarweb.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape SimilarWeb Website Traffic Analytics](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-similarweb)
- **Code:** [`similarweb.py`](similarweb.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Website pages](results/websites.json) · [Website compare pages](results/websites_compare.json) · [Trend pages](results/trends.json) · [Sitemaps](results/sitemap_urls.json)

## What it scrapes

- Similarweb.com website pages for website traffic inisghts
- Similarweb.com website comparing pages for comparing insights
- Similarweb.com website trend pages for trending websites data
- Similarweb.com sitemaps for urls

## Functions

- `scrape_website(domains)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape website inights from website pages
- `scrape_website_compare(first_domain, second_domain)` → `Dict`: parse website comparing data from similarweb comparing pages
- `scrape_sitemaps(url)` → `List[str]`: scrape link data from bestbuy sitemap
- `scrape_trendings(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: parse trending websites data

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import similarweb


async def main():
    website = await similarweb.scrape_website(domains=["google.com", "twitter.com"])
    website_compare = await similarweb.scrape_website_compare(
        first_domain="twitter.com",
        second_domain="instagram.com",
    )
    sitemaps = await similarweb.scrape_sitemaps(url="https://www.similarweb.com/blog/post-sitemap2.xml")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/websites.json`](results/websites.json): `interests`, `competitors`, `searchesSource`, `incomingReferrals`, `adsSource`, `socialNetworksSource`, `outgoingReferrals`, `compareCompetitor`, `technologies`, `recentAds`, `snapshotDate`, `domain`, `icon`, `previewDesktop`, `previewMobile`, `isInvalidTrafficData`, `domainGaStatus`, `isDataFromGaHighlyDiscrepant`, `isDataFromGa`, `categoryId`, `overview`, `traffic`, `trafficSources`, `ranking`, `demographics`, `geography`
- [`results/websites_compare.json`](results/websites_compare.json): `twitter.com`, `instagram.com`
- [`results/trends.json`](results/trends.json): `name`, `url`, `list`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`similarweb.py`](similarweb.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/similarweb-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_website_scraping`, `test_website_compare_scraping`, `test_trend_scraping`, `test_sitemap_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
